summary: A public Instagram summons now reaches Nora: she hears it from the bridge's event stream when a comment tags her, instead of polling a notification feed that never carried those mentions.
details: The instagram-bridge sends a summons event when a comment tagging her arrives as a DM card; Nora finds the summoner's own comment on the post (written by the card's sender and tagging @noraexample, the newest if several) and answers under it, once, through the same guarded write as before.
Each summons is claimed on the card's message id before anything is read, and one comment gets one reply however many cards point at it.

A card whose post the bridge could not identify is recorded as unresolved and never answered; a malformed one is counted and dropped. With [social.instagram.summons] off, cards are counted and dropped.
Summonses are worked one at a time; the consumer still backs off up to 30 minutes when the session needs a human or the bridge is reconnecting.
Needs migration 0067_summons_message_key. poll_seconds is still accepted in config.toml and is read by nothing.
limitations: Two summonses by the same person under one post resolve to their newest tagging comment, so only one of them is answered.
A summons comment that is not on the first page of the post's comments is not answered.
